title: Opportunistic KV window sampler and decay-driven reshuffle for paged-attention
creator: Anita Shah
description:
Problem statement: In high-concurrency multi-tenant workloads we observe noisy KV cache residency leading to decode stalls and elevated P95 latencies. Existing eviction heuristics are conservative LRU-like windows that either over-evict hot spans or hold cold fragments too long, which degrades throughput and increases kernel context switches. Goal: introduce an opportunistic window sampling + decay-driven reshuffle that biases reclaim toward low-value spans while preserving contiguous run-lengths for kernel-friendly prefill. The feature should: 1) reduce decode tail latency (P95) by >10% on mixed workloads, 2) lower token compute overhead due to kernel churn by ~7% (metric: kernel-switches/token), and 3) avoid regressions in throughput for enterprise tenants with reserved capacity.

Design summary: Implement a lightweight sampler that periodically probes a small set of KV windows (configurable window_size_ms) using amortized bloom filters and last-touch decay scores. Each KV span maintains a compact touch histogram (4 buckets) and an affinity score for preferred kernel placement (small/large kernel). The sampler computes a reclaim_score = decay_weight * age_score + touch_entropy_penalty + kernel_mismatch_penalty + tenant_penalty. Spans with reclaim_score above a dynamic threshold are prioritized for reshuffle/compaction. Reshuffle operations try to coalesce adjacent low-score fragments to create contiguous pages that match the preferred kernel tile sizes, enabling more efficient prefill and lower kernel-switch overhead.

Prefill/decode scheduling integration: The sampler feeds a prefill admission controller. If many contiguous pages are available for a request's prefix, the controller will prefill them aggressively and route the request to a kernel variant optimized for longer sequences. For requests without contiguous spans, the controller prefers smaller kernel paths and gradual decode to avoid large cold physical reads.

Kernel selection interplay: Kernel selector will be extended with a new signal 'contiguity_score' derived from the sampler's compaction readiness. The runtime will favor fused kernels when contiguity_score >= threshold_fused. This reduces per-token kernel switching and allows batched decode windows to be processed with fewer kernel invocations.

Simulations and early results: We ran a 48-hour simulation using traces from two production clusters (mixed-chat and instruction-fine-tune). With conservative sampler params (window_probe_rate=0.05, decay_half_life=6h) we observed: - Chat cluster: P95 decode latency down 12.3%, kernel-switches/token down 8.0%, throughput stable +/-1.1% - Instruction cluster: P95 down 9.1%, kernel-switches/token down 6.5%, throughput +0.7% Memory overhead: ~1.4% extra metadata (histogram + affinity). Risk: aggressive compaction increased short-lived tenant tail for micro-bursts in synthetic tests; mitigated by tenant_penalty and soft-quarantine window in design.

Implementation plan: 1) metadata layout change (compact 32-bit histogram + 8-bit affinity) + migration path that backfills lazily, 2) sampler service inside runtime per-GPU node with async reshape worker, 3) prefill admission controller extension, 4) kernel selector patch to consume contiguity_score, 5) metrics and traces (kernel-switches/token, contiguity_ratio, compaction_ops/sec), 6) canary rollout on staging/dedicated-reserved pool.

Instrumentation and observability: Add events and counters: sampler.probed_windows, sampler.reclaimed_bytes, sampler.compactions, kernel.contiguity_score_histogram, admission.prefill_hit_rate. Dashboards: contiguity heatmap per-tenant, prefill success rate, regression alerts when P99 increases >5% during rollout.

Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end tests and unit tests for histogram math and thresholding - Simulator reproduces improvements with no throughput regression across 3 trace families - Staging canary shows <=2% error rate increase and P95 improvement >=8% before broad rollout - Feature flag with runtime knobs for probe rate, decay, tenant_penalty

QA / Test plan: - Synthetic micro-bursts to validate soft-quarantine avoids regressions - Fault injection (worker crash/restart) to verify lazy backfill doesn’t block runtime - Long-running soak (72h) on low-latency cluster to ensure metadata GC and no memory leaks - A/B canary with 5% traffic on Dedicated pool, monitor kernel-switches/token and P95

Rollout steps: 1) merge metadata and sampler behind feature flag, 2) enable sampler in staging for 100% traffic, run soak and gather metrics, 3) canary 5% on dedicated-reserved for 48h, 4) expand to 25% with hour-by-hour monitors, 5) full rollout with adjustable probe_rate parameters.

Backward compatibility and migration: metadata uses on-disk backward-compatible compact encoding. New runtime falls back to existing LRU windows if metadata absent. Migration worker marks pages after first-touch; we will monitor migration rate and memory increase with a runtime gauge.

Related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Opportunistic+KV+Window+Sampler GitHub RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/238 GitHub implementation draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8176
